game: Week 5 DEN@LAC / kickoff not in pack / spread not saved / total not saved / weather not saved

script.base: Spread and total were not saved, so this is form-only and not a market script. Base case is competitive, not a blowout: LAC's offense is Hampton-led (47 carries, 195 rush yards over weeks 2-4) with Harris as the downfield piece, and DEN is Dobbins on the ground (38/125, 3.29 YPC) plus Waddle through the air (24 targets, 183 rec yards). DEN is the softer defense (5.02 rush YPC allowed, 15 runs of 10+, middle 9.09 YPA) and the aggressor (39% blitz). LAC is tighter vs the run (4.13 YPC) and the middle (6.07 YPA), leaks outside (left 8.42, right 8.68), and blitzes only 27%. Most likely flow: both lead backs get their carries, DEN's blitz bothers Herbert (-0.32 EPA vs blitz), and Nix is not forced off schedule often enough for a pure checkdown game.
script.flip1: DEN leads early and runs clock. Dobbins carry count jumps, LAC abandons Hampton, Herbert throws into a 39% blitz he has failed (-0.32 EPA, n=35), and Harris's air-yard game (206 air yards on 15 targets) stalls.
script.flip2: LAC leads and DEN chases. Dobbins's already thin rush efficiency dies, Nix throws more to Waddle (264 air yards), Harvey's receiving role rises, and Hampton can still grind if the Chargers protect the lead.

Harris (206 air yards) runs into DEN's 39% blitz and Herbert's -0.32 EPA vs blitz, so the deep overlap is a trap, not a leg.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Hampton is the Chargers' carry share (47 rushes, 195 yards, 65 a game over the last three) running into the defense in this pack that actually leaks the run (Denver 5.02 YPC allowed, 15 runs of 10+), and 41.5 sits about 23 yards under that role.
edge_players.must_be_true: He plays a full lead-back workload near 12-16 carries, Denver's run leak shows up again, and the game does not become a pass-only blowout before he gets volume. No injury or inactive note in the pack.
edge_players.kills_it: LAC falls way behind early, abandons the run, and Mitchell/Herbert take what's left, or a snap limit we do not have. A mild negative script still clears 41.5; only a real abandonment kills it.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Harvey is a receiver in this offense, not a rusher: 9 carries and 31 yards over three games versus 17 targets and 109 receiving yards, so 26.5 rush yards prices a role he does not have, and even LAC's 4.13 YPC on a 3-carry share is about 12 yards.
edge_players.must_be_true: Dobbins keeps the early-down work (38 carries over L3) and Harvey stays around 3 carries as the checkdown back. He is healthy enough to play that receiving role.
edge_players.kills_it: Dobbins is limited or out (inactives not in the pack) and Harvey's carries spike, or one 20-yard run plus his normal 10 yards clears 26.5 on skew.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and the slip lost because the missing spread was a Denver favorite and the game was never competitive: Chargers trailed early, Hampton was held to 8-10 carries and finished in the mid-30s while Mitchell vultured the rest, and Harvey ripped one 20-yard gain on a light carry count to clear 26.5 on skew alone. The other miss path is an inactive we did not have, Dobbins down and Harvey suddenly a 8-10 carry back. Denver's 5.02 YPC allowed is only four games and may be opponent noise, not a stable leak. That counter is real but not stronger than a 23-yard cushion on the lead back, so Hampton stays; Harvey stays only as a lean because the splash-run kill is live.
slip_story: One story: LAC can run on this Denver defense, and Denver's RB2 does not become a rusher. Hampton rush over is the run-leak leg and survives the base and a moderate LAC-lead flip. Harvey rush under belongs to the same card because his job is targets, not carries, in a competitive game or a Denver chase; it is not a shootout stack and it is not paired with a total or a TD. Do not add Harris over, Gadsden over, or Dobbins over — those need the opposite pressure or clock-kill script.
